name: ClubAL
summary: Windows software to record routines, publish what displays need and provide read-only access.
promise: Record on the PC, publish to displays and provide access without editing.
imageAlt: Current ClubAL Rotinas PEMSE interface with fictional data, schedule, operating hours and weather

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Operational information gets lost when every environment improvises.
tabs.body: Spreadsheets, paper and scattered messages create different versions of the same routine. ClubAL centralizes records on the responsible PC and separates editing from reading.

tabs.label: Three modules
tabs.title: Each module handles one part of the work.
tabs.body: Operação PEMSE records and publishes; Rotinas PEMSE displays only approved information; Consulta PEMSE provides authorized reading without opening editing.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The product can be demonstrated and deployment remains assisted.
tabs.body: Windows flows, offline mode and publishing rules have automated validation. Physical installations, displays and networks still require human acceptance.
points: Windows packages are not code-signed yet

promise: Dun Caerwyn: blood, memory and choices that leave marks.

tabs.label: Game
tabs.title: An adult protagonist in a world that records consequences.
tabs.body: Maeve crosses Dun Caerwyn, House Roscaern and systems where body, blood and memory affect narrative and combat.

tabs.label: Production
tabs.title: The scale is designed for one person to finish.
tabs.body: Compact areas, modular kits and concentrated detail preserve the mood without promising a world larger than solo production can support.

tabs.label: The Architect
tabs.title: The creator appears as a possible entity in the world.
tabs.body: Gui as The Architect is a conceptual easter egg about authorship and consequence. It inspires the project without claiming an implemented character.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The first combat slice has a technical foundation.
tabs.body: Light combo, dodge and Blood First are part of Phase 8. Automated gates passed; human gameplay acceptance remains pending.

name: Demonyza
kicker: Digital presence case for a content creator
summary: A case bringing together a content creator’s profile, schedule, streams and community.
promise: One home for content, schedule and community.
imageAlt: Current Demonyza homepage with purple visual identity, navigation and interactive areas

tabs.label: Challenge
tabs.title: More than a link page.
tabs.body: The site needed to introduce the creator, organize public channels and give the community easy routes without erasing the client’s identity.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: The client’s identity, with clear navigation.
tabs.body: The responsive experience brings together profile, schedule, Twitch, Discord and OpenDota in an original interface for mobile and desktop.
points: Easy return to the main flow

tabs.label: Delivery
tabs.title: Live and maintained independently.
tabs.body: The site is live on Cloudflare Pages. The client’s code remains protected in a private repository.

name: Codex Checkpoint
kicker: A local queue for human validation
summary: A local queue that preserves pending tests, decisions and feedback across agent-assisted work sessions.
promise: The agent records it. A person validates when available. Context remains.
imageAlt: Codex Checkpoint showing a fictional queue of human validations and note history

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Not every test can be completed during the session.
tabs.body: Gameplay, visual review, devices, authentication and practical decisions depend on a person or another environment. Without a queue, that context disappears.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A validation queue — not another chat.
tabs.body: The agent records the checkpoint; Gui returns when available and leaves a decision or actionable feedback.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A native, installable application.
tabs.body: Interface, command line and file integration form the product. Current builds are not code-signed yet, and that remains clearly stated.

name: NEXUS
kicker: A Windows hub for local projects
summary: A Windows hub for opening projects, resources and checks from a local catalog.
imageAlt: NEXUS showing ClubAL and local actions for Operação, Rotinas and Consulta

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Local projects accumulate scattered shortcuts, scripts and instructions.
tabs.body: When every product has its own runtime, finding the right action becomes work before the work.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A command desk managed by a catalog.
tabs.body: Each card presents actions, references and checks without mixing product runtimes.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A local development tool.
tabs.body: Build, self-test and rendering are reproducible. NEXUS organizes work on the computer; it is not embedded in product runtimes.

name: Local First Checklist
summary: An open-source Python application with a local JSON checklist, command line, tests and CI.
promise: A compact example of local-first software.
imageAlt: Illustration of a local checklist with completed items and a JSON file

tabs.label: Scope
tabs.title: Small enough to understand end to end.
tabs.body: Tasks live in a local JSON file and simple operations are available through the command line.

tabs.label: Quality
tabs.title: Simplicity still needs evidence.
tabs.body: Unit tests, Python compilation and a smoke test protect the main operations without adding infrastructure to the application.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: Version 1.0.0 is published.
tabs.body: The repository demonstrates structure, documentation, tests and a coherent architectural choice in a limited scope.
